text: Doctor, one item is left on the survey plan, if you want it. It is optional. A ranging-laser test at the photon sphere.

title: Optional: take the Tern down to the photon sphere, 1.5 rₛ (helm)

text: One and a half horizon radii. At that height light can orbit Erebus. A beam fired sideways goes all the way round.
Light going in a circle. Okay, doc, I have to see that.
Photon sphere. I have locked the field to it, to within a centimetre. You will see why that matters.
Look forward: the shadow now covers exactly half the sky, 180 degrees. Its edge is a circle at right angles to our nose: straight up, straight down, and straight out on either side of the hull.
The helm is the low desk in the middle of the bridge. Lower the altitude to 1.500 rₛ and the field will lock there.

title: Optional: take the Tern down to the photon sphere, 1.5 rₛ (helm)
Fire the ranging laser along the hull (helm)

text: Pulse away. Watch the plot on the helm panel.
Caught at the stern, 11.1 seconds after it left, 2.7 metres from where it set out. It went all the way round Erebus: 3.34 million km.
As you predicted. That is just the circumference divided by the speed of light.
Wait. So any light that leaves the ship sideways comes back round to us?
Exactly sideways, yes. Including the light bouncing off the back of your head.
So if I look straight along the hull, right at the edge of the shadow...

You see the back of your own head, as it was 11 seconds ago. Squeezed into a thin line along the edge. One more lap in, a second copy, 22 seconds old and hundreds of times thinner. The hull camera on the helm panel looks along it.
That is the creepiest thing I've heard all week. And I nearly fell into a black hole this morning.
Now the reason for the centimetre. The dorsal mast has a laser too, one metre further out. Fire it and watch.

title: Fire the ranging laser along the hull (helm)
Fire a pulse from the mast, one metre further out (helm)

text: Lap one: it passed us 268 metres too high. It missed the stern.
The second laser button on the helm panel fires from the dorsal mast, one metre further from Erebus.
